transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I keep getting stuck on these ideas that people around me are plotting or judging me, even when they swear they aren’t. It's been causing a lot of tension at my job and with my spouse, so I finally agreed to come talk to someone.
Do you feel there is a specific, active conspiracy or plan to harm or trick you, or is it more of a constant worry that people are judging and criticizing you?

It started out as just a constant worry that people were judging or criticizing me, but now it really feels like an active plan behind my back. For instance, when my supervisor took me off a big EV job, I became convinced he and my husband had teamed up and decided I couldn't be trusted, and I still can't shake that feeling even though they both swear it's not true.
Besides these thoughts about others plotting against you, have you ever heard voices, seen things, or had other sensory experiences that others didn't seem to notice?

Yes, I do sometimes hear a man's voice, especially when I'm working late in the garage or alone at home. It comments on what I'm doing, saying things like "They're laughing at you" or "You're wasting your time." Even though I hear it clear as day, I know there isn't actually anyone there.
How long have you been hearing this voice, and how often does it happen during the week?
It’s been going on since late last fall, so for about a year now. I hear it every so often, maybe a few times a week, mostly when I'm working by myself or alone in the house.
During this past year, have you experienced any periods of feeling very down and depressed, or on the other hand, unusually energetic and hyperactive?

Yes, I've experienced both extremes over this past year. I'll go through these highly energetic "up" phases where I feel wired, stay up late working on projects, and can't sit still, but then I'll crash into low phases where I just sit on the couch staring at the TV and struggle to even shower.
Do you hear these voices or have these paranoid thoughts even during times when your mood feels completely normal, or do they only happen when you are in those 'up' or 'down' phases?

Yes, I actually do experience them even when my mood is completely normal. This past spring, my mood had flattened out and I wasn't feeling especially up or down, but for a few weeks I still kept hearing that man's voice and felt convinced people at work were plotting against me.

When you have these 'up' and 'down' phases, do they usually happen at separate times, or have you ever experienced them both at the same time—like feeling extremely energetic and wired while also feeling deeply sad or hopeless?

No, they usually happen at separate times rather than at the same time. When I'm in those "up" phases, I might get really irritated or snap at people, but I don't feel sad or hopeless until I crash into those low periods.
How long do these 'up' and 'down' phases typically last? Do they stay the same for weeks or months, or do they rapidly switch back and forth within a few days?

The "up" phases definitely last for weeks at a time rather than shifting back and forth in just a few days. I'll have weeks where I barely sleep for more than three or four hours a night but still feel completely wired and energized. These periods have been coming and going like that for close to a year now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic and wired, but at the exact same time felt deeply sad, hopeless, or empty, lasting for at least several days?

No, I haven't really experienced feeling wired and deeply sad or hopeless at the exact same time. My high-energy periods and my low, unmotivated periods usually seem to happen at completely different times.
To help me rule out other potential causes, do you regularly use alcohol, recreational drugs, or take any prescription medications?
No, I don't regularly drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs. I'm also not taking any prescription medications right now.
During those "up" phases when you feel wired and barely sleep, do you also experience things like your thoughts racing incredibly fast, talking much faster than usual, or taking unusual risks?

Yes, my mind races constantly during those times, especially when I'm lying awake at night. My wife and coworkers also tell me that I talk incredibly fast and constantly jump from one topic to another. I don't really feel like I take dangerous or unusual risks, but the racing thoughts and fast talking are definitely very prominent.
Looking back over this past year, would you say these high and low mood phases have been present for most of the total time you've been dealing with these struggles, or just a small part of it?

Yes, looking back over this past year, those high-energy, wired phases—or recovering and coming down from them—have definitely been present for the majority of the time. I've only had very brief stretches where my mood felt relatively normal.

latest_inference.note: The patient presents with both manic and depressive episodes alongside prominent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations of a commenting voice and persecutory delusions). Crucially, the psychotic symptoms persisted for several weeks during a period of euthymia (normal mood), which points away from a primary mood disorder (Bipolar Disorder, F31) and toward a schizoaffective presentation. Since the patient has experienced both manic and depressive phases in addition to the schizophrenic symptoms, F25.2 (Schizoaffective disorder, mixed type) is the most accurate diagnosis. Substance use and medical causes have been ruled out. The clinical picture is complete, allowing for a final diagnosis.
